cases.input: A complex competency may need more than one observation, but there is no justified universal item count.
requiredBehaviors: derive evidence breadth from complexity and error risk
distinguish insufficient evidence from failed evidence
forbiddenBehaviors: invent an unsupported universal minimum item count
equate missing observations with an incorrect answer

cases.input: A draft assessment calls a near-copy of a practiced example a transfer test and uses lesson completion as the main success criterion.
requiredBehaviors: reject lesson completion as competence evidence
reject the near-copy as strong transfer evidence
require observable performance and sufficient novelty
forbiddenBehaviors: promote recall or coverage to transfer
hide the lack of authoritative answer basis
